identity.title: Generation and validation of B2M knockout human iPSC line, LVPEIi001-C-2 that lacks the cell surface expression of HLA-Class I antigens.

content.abstract: MHC Class-I molecules present self antigens to CD8 + T cells and mediate self vs non-self recognition and this mechanism plays a major role in mismatched graft rejections. Beta-2 microglobulin (B2M) binds non-covalently with MHCI heavy chains and stabilizes the peptide-binding groove on cell surfaces. Loss of B2M expression destabilizes the MHCI complexes and could render the cells hypoimmunogenic. Here, we report a B2M(-/-) iPSC line, LVPEIi001-C-2, generated using CRISPR/Cas9-based editing of a healthy control human iPSC line. This line lost the MHCI expression on cell surfaces, retained the stemness, pluripotency, genetic identity, displayed normal karyotype and tested negative for mycoplasma.
